- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +0.50 in sentiment or +10%+ price jump), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add early mean-reversion tail.
- In low-sentiment environments (e.g., sentiment < -0.30), model underestimates downside risk; increase forecast volatility or add 2–3% downward buffer for near-term.
- Model consistently underestimates long-term (30d) price recovery after short-term dips; add 1–2% upward bias in later forecast periods if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment shows early reversal (e.g., from negative to mildly positive), model often lags; shift forecast upward by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to capture sentiment momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion, reduce forecast sensitivity to recent spikes; use 2–3 day smoothing filter for sentiment-driven corrections.
